products.name: Turmeric Powder
products.blurb: Sun-dried and stone-ground for a deep golden hue and an earthy, warm finish.
products.description: Our haldi is sourced from the turmeric belt of Erode and Sangli, sun-dried and stone-ground in small batches so the natural curcumin and aroma stay intact. Deep gold in colour, warm and slightly bitter in the best way — the backbone of every Indian gravy.
products.usage: Add a quarter teaspoon early in the tempering so the raw note cooks out, or whisk into warm milk with a pinch of pepper.

products.name: Red Chilli Powder
products.blurb: Bold heat with a vivid colour, milled from hand-picked dried red chillies.
products.description: Guntur and Byadgi chillies, dried in the sun and milled without any added colour. You get a natural crimson that colours the oil the moment it hits the pan, with a clean heat that builds rather than burns.
products.ingredients: 100% Capsicum annuum (dried red chilli). No added colour.
products.usage: Bloom in hot oil for a tadka, or mix with a little water into a paste so it does not scorch.

products.name: Coriander Powder
products.blurb: Light, citrusy and gently sweet — the cooling counterweight to chilli.
products.description: Round, plump dhaniya with a clean citrus note. Ground fresh, it lifts a masala from flat to fragrant. It is the quiet volume knob on heat — add more to soften a dish without losing depth.
products.usage: Add mid-cook with the other powders; a late addition keeps more of the citrus top note.

products.name: Garam Masala
products.blurb: Our house blend — roasted whole spices, ground together in small batches.
products.description: A balanced blend of coriander, cumin, black pepper, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and bay, dry-roasted and ground together. Warming rather than hot, with a rounded finish that sits behind the dish instead of over it.
products.ingredients: Coriander, cumin, black pepper, green cardamom, cinnamon, clove, bay leaf, nutmeg.
products.usage: Sprinkle in the last two minutes of cooking, or finish a dish off the heat so the aromatics stay bright.

products.name: Kitchen King Masala
products.blurb: The all-rounder for everyday sabzi — one spoon, no guesswork.
products.description: Built for the nights when you want one masala and a good result. Roasted spice base with a gentle sweetness from onion and kasuri methi notes, tuned so it works across aloo, gobhi, paneer and mixed veg.
products.ingredients: Coriander, red chilli, cumin, turmeric, dry mango, kasuri methi, black salt, spices.
products.usage: One heaped teaspoon per four servings, added once the vegetables are half done.

products.name: Chana Masala
products.blurb: Tangy, dark and full-bodied — built for chole that taste like the street.
products.description: Amchur and anardana give the sourness that makes good chole, backed by roasted cumin and a slow-building chilli heat. Dark in colour because the spices are roasted, not because anything is added.
products.ingredients: Coriander, cumin, red chilli, dry mango, pomegranate seed, black salt, clove, bay leaf.
products.usage: Add after the onion-tomato base has cooked down, then simmer the chickpeas in it for at least ten minutes.

products.name: Sambar Masala
products.blurb: South-Indian style, with roasted dal and curry leaf in the blend.
products.description: Roasted chana dal and toor dal give the body that makes a sambar taste finished. Curry leaf, fenugreek and a hint of jaggery round off the heat, so it works with both vegetables and drumstick.
products.ingredients: Coriander, red chilli, roasted chana dal, toor dal, fenugreek, curry leaf, turmeric, asafoetida.
products.usage: Stir into the cooked dal-vegetable mix and simmer five minutes before the final tempering.

products.name: Pav Bhaji Masala
products.blurb: Smoky, tangy and a little sharp — the Mumbai street-stall profile.
products.description: Fennel and black salt carry the top note, with amchur for the tang and a slow chilli warmth underneath. Built to stand up to butter and mashed vegetables without disappearing.
products.ingredients: Coriander, red chilli, fennel, cumin, dry mango, black salt, cinnamon, clove, black pepper.
products.usage: Add to the mashed vegetables with a generous knob of butter and cook until the oil separates.

products.name: Jeera Whole
products.blurb: Nutty, aromatic and deeply warming — the quiet backbone of Indian cooking.
products.description: Cleaned and graded jeera with a high volatile-oil content. Toast it in ghee and the whole kitchen knows. We pack it whole because that is how it keeps its aroma longest.
products.usage: Dry-roast or bloom in hot ghee until it crackles, then proceed. Ground fresh as needed.

products.name: Black Pepper
products.blurb: Tellicherry-grade peppercorns with a sharp, complex bite.
products.description: Large Tellicherry-grade peppercorns from the Malabar coast, vine-ripened for a fuller flavour and higher piperine content. Sharper and more layered than standard pepper.
products.usage: Crack fresh over a finished dish. For curries, add whole corns early so they soften into the gravy.

products.name: Green Cardamom
products.blurb: Plump, aromatic pods — sweet, floral and unmistakable.
products.description: Hand-sorted 8 mm green cardamom pods with a bright, almost menthol sweetness. A little goes a long way, which is why we sell it in smaller packs.
products.usage: Crush a pod or two into chai or kheer. For biryani, add whole pods to the rice before the lid goes on.

products.name: Cloves
products.blurb: Fat, oil-rich buds with a deep, numbing warmth.
products.description: Whole cloves with the head still intact — the sign of a bud picked at the right time. Strong enough that one or two is usually all a dish needs.
products.usage: Add whole to rice, gravies and chai. Pull them out before serving.

products.name: Cinnamon Sticks
products.blurb: Warm, sweet bark — quills that snap clean and smell of the forest.
products.description: Thin, tightly rolled quills with a sweet woody warmth. Break a piece and the aroma should hit immediately — that is the volatile oil you are paying for.
products.usage: Snap into rice, biryani and slow-cooked gravies. Also good in a winter chai.

products.name: Star Anise
products.blurb: Whole eight-point stars with a deep liquorice warmth.
products.description: Intact, well-formed stars with a strong anethole note. Essential in Chettinad and Bengali cooking, and a natural pairing with cinnamon and clove in our garam masala.
products.usage: One star is plenty for a family-sized pot. Add early so it has time to infuse.

products.name: Bay Leaf
products.blurb: Whole dried leaves with a clean, herbal bite.
products.description: Whole leaves, not crushed fragments. They hold their shape through a long cook and release a soft, tea-like aroma that rounds off a gravy.
products.usage: Drop into hot oil at the start of a curry, or add to rice before cooking.

products.name: Mustard Seeds
products.blurb: Small, dark and sharp — the crackle at the start of a South-Indian tadka.
products.description: Tiny black mustard seeds that pop the moment they hit hot oil. The sound is the cue — once they crackle, the oil is seasoned and ready.
products.usage: Heat oil, add seeds, wait for the crackle, then add curry leaf and the rest.

products.name: Fenugreek Seeds
products.blurb: Bitter, maple-sweet seeds — a little goes a very long way.
products.description: Hard, angular methi dana with the characteristic bitter-sweet note. Roasted and ground, it is what gives a sambar or pickle its backbone.
products.usage: Roast lightly before grinding — raw seeds are harsh. Use sparingly.

combos.blurb: Six spices that between them cover almost every Indian kitchen.
combos.description: The full starter shelf in one box. Six 100 g jars — everything you reach for on a normal weekday, nothing you will not finish.

combos.name: Everyday Masala Combo
combos.blurb: Five blends for the dishes you actually cook on repeat.
combos.description: If you cook a rotation of five or six dishes, this is the shortcut. One spoon of the right blend instead of measuring six powders every night.

combos.name: Golden Trio
combos.blurb: Haldi, mirchi, dhaniya — the three that start almost everything.
combos.description: The base of nearly every Indian gravy, in one small box. The cheapest way to try MJ MASALA if you have never ordered before.

combos.name: Whole Spice Starter
combos.blurb: Four whole spices to grind your own blends at home.
combos.description: For anyone who has decided to grind their own garam masala. Whole spices keep their oils far longer than powder — buy once, grind as you go.

combos.name: Daily Cooking Combo

combos.name: Haldi + Mirchi Duo

combos.description: The smallest way to start. Two jars, both of which you will finish — which is more than can be said for most sampler packs.
